p0.original: 关键问题：心理学的6个主要视角是什么
p0.en: Key issues: What are the six main perspectives of psychology?

p2.original: 现代心理学由6个主要视角构成，它们是生物视角、认知视角、行为视角、全人视角、发展视角和社会文化视角，每个视角都发展出了有关心智和行为的全新概念。
p2.en: Modern psychology consists of six main perspectives: biological, cognitive, behavioural, human, developmental and sociocultural, each of which develops a whole new concept of mental and behavioural.

p3.original: 心理学的历史可以追溯到古希腊的哲学家苏格拉底、柏拉图和亚里士多德，是这些历史人物塑造了现代心理学的雏形。他们不仅对意识和疯狂行为做出了思考，而且还发现情绪能够扭曲思维，认为人们的感知只是对外部世界的解读。即使在今天，人们可能依然认同许多这些古老的猜测，而现代心理学也是如此。
p3.en: The history of psychology dates back to the ancient Greek philosophers Socrates, Plato and Aristotle, who were the first to shape modern psychology. Not only did they reflect on consciousness and madness, but they also found emotions that distorted thinking, thinking that people's perception was only an interpretation of the outside world. Even today, one may still agree with many of these old speculations, as does modern psychology.

p4.original: 但古希腊人在奠定心理学基础方面只占得一席之地。差不多在同一时期，亚洲和非洲社会也在发展自己的心理学思想。在亚洲，瑜伽的追随者和佛教信徒在探索意识的奥妙，他们试图通过冥想来控制意识。与此同时，在非洲，人们用精神信仰对人格和精神障碍提出了其他解释（Berry et al.，1992）。然而，西方心理学作为一门科学，有着曲折的发展道路，对它的发展影响最大的还是古希腊的传统，以及后来的天主教会。
p4.en: But the ancient Greeks had only a place to lay the foundations of psychology. Almost during the same period, Asian and African societies are also developing their own psychology. In Asia, Yoga followers and Buddhists are exploring the wonders of consciousness, which they try to control through meditation. At the same time, in Africa, other interpretations of personality and mental disorder are offered with spirituality (Berry et al., 1992). Western psychology, however, as a science, has a twisted path of development, which has the greatest impact on its development, as has the ancient Greek tradition and, later, the Catholic Church.

p5.original: 教会在影响心理学研究方面发挥了哪些作用呢？比如，在中世纪，教会极力压制人们对人类本性的探索，在一定程度上压抑了人类对“欲望世界”的兴趣。中世纪的基督徒认为，人类的心理和灵魂是不可分割的——就像上帝的心理一样——是凡人永远无法解开的谜。
p5.en: What role does the Church play in influencing psychological research? In the Middle Ages, for example, the Church has been trying to suppress the exploration of the nature of the human being, to a certain extent, the interest of the human race in the world of desire. Middle-century Christians believe that the human mind and soul are inseparable — just like the mind of God — a mystery that mortals will never solve.

p6.original: 改变这种在人们头脑中根深蒂固的观点殊为不易。之后的几百年中，历经了一系列激进的新观点的冲击，中世纪的思维定式才被打破，并且奠定了现代心理学的知识基础——为我们带来了这一部分的核心概念：
p6.en: It is not easy to change this deep-rooted view in people's minds. In the centuries that followed, after the shock of a series of radical new ideas, medieval mindsets were broken and the knowledge base of modern psychology was laid down — bringing to us the core concept of this part:

p7.original: 现代心理学由6个主要视角构成，它们是生物视角、认知视角、行为视角、全人视角、发展视角和社会文化视角，每个视角都发展出了有关心智和行为的全新概念。
p7.en: Modern psychology consists of six main perspectives: biological, cognitive, behavioural, human, developmental and sociocultural, each of which develops a whole new concept of mental and behavioural.

p8.original: 当我们探讨这些视角时，你会看到每个视角都为人类行为提供了自己独特的解释。综合起来，它们构成了心理学的多元视角，每一个视角都成了我们理解人类行为的“心理学工具箱”中的重要工具。为了帮助你了解这些视角是多么有用，我们将把每一个视角运用到一个令许多学生苦恼的问题上：拖延症。让我们先从生物视角开始吧。
p8.en: As we explore these perspectives, you will see that each of them provides its own unique interpretation of human behaviour. Taken together, they constitute a multifaceted perspective of psychology, each of which has become an important tool in our “psychological toolbox” of understanding of human behaviour. In order to help you understand how useful these perspectives are, we will apply each of them to an issue that is troubling many students: delay. Let's start with a biological perspective.

p11.original: 1.4 描述科学心理学和现代认知视角的发展史。
p11.en: 1.4 Describe the history of the development of scientific psychology and modern cognitive perspectives.

p12.original: 1.5 总结在20世纪出现的心理学视角。
p12.en: 1.5 Summarizing the psychological perspective that emerged in the twentieth century.

p13.original: 1.6 将心理学视角应用于自己的行为。
p13.en: 1.6 Psychological perspectives are applied to their own behaviour.

p17.original: 17世纪的法国哲学家笛卡儿（René Descartes）提出了第一个激进新概念，即身心二元论，这一概念首次且最终引出了现代心理学。笛卡儿提出这一观点的天才之处在于，它使教会不再限制科学家对心理的科学研究，同时也允许其对人类的感觉和行为进行研究，因为它们都建立在神经系统的物理活动的基础之上。他的观点与当时生物学界一些令人振奋的新发现非常吻合，科学家刚刚研究出动物的感觉器官如何将刺激转化为神经冲动和肌肉反应。这类发现和笛卡儿的身心分离的观点结合在一起，让科学家得以证明，引发感觉和简单反射行为的是生物过程，而非神秘的精神力量。
p17.en: The 17th century French philosopher René Descartes introduced the first radical new concept, the dualism of mind and mind, which led to modern psychology for the first time and eventually. The genius of Descartes in raising this view is that it removes the Church from limiting the scientific research of psychology by scientists, and at the same time allows them to study the perception and behaviour of human beings, which are based on the physical activities of the nervous system. His point of view was very consistent with some exciting new discoveries in biology at the time, and scientists had just studied how the sensory organs of animals turned stimulation into neuro-morbid and muscular reactions. Such discoveries, combined with the idea of the physical and psychological separation of Cartesian, have enabled scientists to prove that it is biological processes, not mysterious spiritual forces, that trigger sensory and simple reflexes.

p19.original: 在400年后，笛卡儿的革命性视角为现代生物视角（biological perspective）奠定了基础。不过，现代生物心理学家不再受中世纪教会的限制，他们重新把心理和身体联系起来（尽管他们把灵魂的问题留给了宗教），现在他们把心理看作大脑的产物。
p19.en: After 400 years, Cartesian's revolutionary perspective has laid the foundation for modern biological perspective. However, modern biopsychologists are no longer restricted by medieval churches, reconnecting their mental and physical (although they leave their spiritual problems to religion) and now view psychology as the creation of the brain.

p20.original: 心理学中的生物视角试图从我们的大脑和神经系统中寻找人类行为的起因。神经科学和进化心理学都是生物视角的分支。
p20.en: The biological perspective of psychology attempts to find the causes of human behaviour in our brain and nervous system. Neuroscience and evolutionary psychology are all branches of the biological perspective.

p21.original: 按照目前的这种观点，我们的人格、偏好、行为模式和能力都源于我们的身体结构。因此，生物心理学家往往从大脑、神经系统、内分泌系统和基因中寻找我们行为产生的原因。从这个角度来看，拖延问题可能是源于某种大脑化学物质的作用（Liu et al.，2004），可能具有遗传性。虽然生物心理学家并不否认关于心理和行为的其他视角的价值，但他们却旨在尽可能多地了解心理过程的身体基础。
p21.en: According to the current view, our personality, preferences, patterns of behaviour and abilities all derive from our physical structure. As a result, biopsychologists tend to look for the causes of our behaviour from the brain, the nervous system, the endocrine system and genes. From this point of view, the problem of delay may be a function of a certain brain chemical substance (Liu et al., 2004) and may be genetic. While biopsychiatrics do not deny the value of other perspectives on psychology and behaviour, they aim to gain as much understanding as possible of the physical basis of the psychological process.

p22.en: 1.3.2 Two variants from a biological perspective

p23.original: 和你想象的一样，生物视角在医学和生物科学中有着牢固的根基。新兴的神经科学（neuroscience）综合了生物心理学、生物学、神经学和其他对大脑运作机制感兴趣的学科。感谢计算机及脑成像技术的惊人发展，神经科学已经成了一个热门的研究领域。在该领域的成果中，神经科学家已经知晓特定部位的损伤会如何破坏特定的能力，比如，语言能力、社交技能或记忆力。神经科学和脑影像还揭示了隐秘的睡眠与梦境世界、药物对大脑的影响，以及其他的意识状态。
p23.en: As you can imagine, the biological perspective has a strong foundation in medicine and bioscience. The emerging neuroscience combines biopsychology, biology, neurology and other disciplines interested in the mechanisms of brain operation. Thanks to the dramatic development of computer and brain imaging technologies, neuroscience has become a popular field of research. Among the results in this area, neuroscientists already know how damage to particular areas can undermine specific capabilities, such as language skills, social skills or memory. Neural science and brain images also reveal the hidden world of sleep and dreams, the effects of drugs on the brain, and other state of consciousness.

p24.original: 生物心理学的另一个重要变体萌芽于大约150年前查尔斯·达尔文（Charles Darwin）所提出的观点。进化心理学（evolutionary psychology）认为，人类的许多行为都源于遗传倾向，近年遗传学研究成果的激增也极大地促进了这一领域的发展。从进化的观点来看，在我们最根深蒂固的行为下的基因结构，是由几千年前我们祖先所面临的生存条件造就的。
p24.en: Another important variant of biopsychology was born out of a point made by Charles Darwin some 150 years ago. Evolutionary psychology believes that many human behaviour is rooted in genetic tendencies and that the proliferation of recent genetic research has contributed significantly to development in this field. From an evolutionary point of view, the genetic structure of our deepest behaviour was created by the conditions of existence that our ancestors faced thousands of years ago.

p25.original: 根据进化心理学的观点，环境的力量像剪刀一样修剪了人类的谱系，让那些具有最适应环境的心理和身体特质的个体生存并繁衍。达尔文将这一过程称为自然选择（natural selection）。通过这一过程，物种的生理特征会向那些提供了竞争优势的生理特征进化。我们人类先进的语言系统，一想到配偶的不忠就会感到的嫉妒，以及在发生冲突时倾向于和家人结盟，都提高了我们生存、繁衍和延续血统的能力，而这些只不过是进化心理学视角的几个例子。
p25.en: According to evolutionary psychology, the power of the environment, like scissors, trims the human spectrum, allowing individuals with the most adaptable psychological and physical characteristics to survive and reproduce. Darwin calls this process natural choice. Through this process, biological characteristics of species evolve to those that offer competitive advantages. Our advanced human language systems, the jealousy that comes with the thought of marital infidelity and the tendency to associate with our families in times of conflict, have enhanced our ability to survive, reproduce and continue our descent, and these are just a few examples of evolutionary psychological perspectives.

p26.original: 然而，进化心理学的一些拥护者提出了一些极具争议性的说法。在他们看来，即使是最恶劣的人类行为，如战争、强奸和杀婴，也可能是从曾经帮助人类适应和生存的生物倾向中生长出来的（Buss，2008）。进化心理学也对某些性别差异提出了生物学解释，比如，为什么男性通常比女性拥有更多的性伴侣。
p26.en: However, some proponents of evolutionary psychology have made very controversial statements. In their view, even the worst human practices, such as war, rape and infanticide, can be born out of biological tendencies that helped humans adapt and survive (Buss, 2008). Evolutionary psychology also offers biological explanations for certain gender differences, such as why men usually have more sexual partners than women.

p27.original: 进化心理学的目的是通过弄清楚早期人类的行为是如何具备适应性（有利于生存）来解释行为。知道了这一点，你能想出一个对于拖延问题的进化心理学角度的解释吗？换句话说，拖延有没有可能通过某种方式帮助早期人类生存和/或繁衍？
p27.en: The aim of evolutionary psychology is to explain behaviour by understanding how early human behaviour is adaptable (for survival). You know, can you come up with an explanation of the evolutionary psychological angle of the delay? In other words, is it possible for delays to contribute in some way to early human survival and/or reproduction?

p30.original: 描述科学心理学和现代认知视角的发展史。
p30.en: Describe the history of the development of scientific psychology and modern cognitive perspectives.

p31.original: 另一个影响早期心理科学的激进观点来自化学领域，化学家们在发现化学元素的性质模式后提出了著名的元素周期表。元素周期表的提出立刻使得元素之间的关系清晰明了。
p31.en: Another radical point of view affecting early psychosciences comes from the chemical field, where chemists, after discovering patterns of the nature of chemical elements, produce well-known periodic tables of elements. The introduction of the periodic table of elements immediately makes the relationship between elements clear.

p32.original: 德国科学家威廉·冯特（Wilhelm Wundt，顺带一提，他是第一个自称为“心理学家”的人）想知道，能否像元素周期表简化化学一样来简化人的心理。或许他能发现意识体验“元素”！尽管冯特没有实现构建心理元素周期表的梦想，但他提出了一个突破性的观点：
p32.en: German scientist Wilhelm Wundt, who, by the way, was the first person to call himself a “psychologist”, wondered whether it would be possible to simplify the human mind like the chemical simplification of the cyclical table of elements. Maybe he can find out about the conscious experience of the Element! Although he did not realize his dream of building a periodic table of psychological elements, he offered a groundbreaking view:

p33.original: 科学当中用来客观地测量和研究自然界的方法，比如，化学方法或物理方法，也可以用来研究心理与身体。
p33.en: Methods used in science to objectively measure and study the natural world, such as chemical or physical methods, can also be used to study the mental and physical.

p34.original: 1.4.1 冯特对意识元素的寻找
p34.en: 1.4.1 vonter's search for elements of consciousness

p35.original: “当你一看到光，请立刻按下按钮。”当冯特教授准备记录光刺激和学生反应之间的反应时间的时候，他可能这样说过。1879年，在位于莱比锡大学（University of Leipzig）的全世界第一个心理学实验室中，这样简单而具体的实验极为常见。在那里，冯特和他的学生还进行了其他一些研究，他们运用一种叫作内省（introspection）的技术，让受过训练的志愿者描述他们对各种刺激的感觉和情绪反应。这是历史上最早的心理学实验：研究冯特和他的学生们提出的意识的基本“元素”，包括感觉、知觉、记忆、注意、情绪、思维、学习和语言（见图1-2）。他们断言，所有的心理活动都是由这些基本过程的不同组合构成的。
p35.en: "When you see the light, press the button immediately. "When Professor Vonter was about to record the reaction time between light irritation and student reaction, he might have said so. In 1879, such simple and specific experiments were very common in the first psychological laboratory in the world, located at the University of Leipzig. There, Vonte and his students also carried out a number of other studies, using a technique called Introspection, which allowed trained volunteers to describe their feelings and emotional reactions to various kinds of irritation. This was the first psychological experiment in history: to study the basic “elements” of the consciousness that Fengt and his students have put forward, including feelings, consciousness, memory, attention, emotions, thinking, learning and language (see figure 1-2). They assert that all psychological activities are made up of different combinations of these basic processes.

p37.original: 冯特的学生爱德华·布拉德福德·铁钦纳（Edward Bradford Titchener）把对意识元素的探索带到了美国，铁钦纳开始把它称为结构主义（structuralism）。铁钦纳创造的术语非常恰当，因为像冯特一样，他的目标也是要揭示出最基本的心理“结构”或成分（Fancher，1979）。因此，尽管冯特从未使用过这个术语，但他被认为是结构主义之父。
p37.en: Edward Bradford Titchener, a student of vonter, brought the exploration of the element of consciousness to the United States, where he began to call it structuralism. The terminology that Tichina has created is very appropriate, because, like Font, his aim is to reveal the most basic psychological “structure” or composition (Fancher, 1979). Thus, although Vonte never used the term, he was considered to be the father of structuralism.

p38.original: 从一开始，冯特和铁钦纳就成了众矢之的。反对意见的矛头直指内省法，认为它过于主观。批评者们问，我们到底如何判断人对其思想与感情的描述的准确性呢？
p38.en: From the beginning, Font and Tinchina were targeted. The objection was directed at internal law and considered it to be too subjective. Critics ask, how exactly do we judge the accuracy of a person's description of his thoughts and feelings?

p39.original: 不过冯特和铁钦纳还是笑到了最后。即使心理学家有时认为他们两个人的观点很古怪，如今相关研究却依然离不开旧的结构主义方法的更新版本。此外，我们想，如果冯特和铁钦纳今天还活着，他们还会有另一个值得开心的理由：如今每一本心理学导论的章节标题里都有这个他们首次确定并探索的主题——也包括本书。在这个“试一试”的环节里亲身体验一下内省吧。
p39.en: But it's the last time Vont and Tiechiner smiled. Even though psychologists sometimes consider their views to be odd, the research still remains an updated version of the old structuralist approach. Moreover, we think that if Fengt and Tiechina were alive today, they would have another reason to be happy: each of the introductory chapters today contains this theme that they have identified and explored for the first time — including this book. In this “try-and-test” section, let's see what we can do.

p40.original: 图1-2 威廉·冯特建立了世界上第一个心理实验室
p40.en: Figure 1-2. William vonter established the first psychological laboratory in the world

p41.original: 注：元素周期表启发了威廉·冯特，促使他思考如何将人类心理分解成类似的基本元素框架。
p41.en: Note: The periodic table of elements inspired William vonter to think about how to decompose the human mind into a similar framework of basic elements.

p42.original: 试一试 内省地观看内克尔立方体
p42.en: Try and see the Nectar Cubic in the interior.

p43.original: 图1-3A中的立方体会捉弄你的眼睛，或者更准确地说，它会捉弄你的大脑。盯着这个立方体看一会儿，你看它的视角会突然改变。有时你好像是从右上角看它（见图1-3B），但过一会儿又好像你从左下角看它（见图1-3C）。
p43.en: The cubes in 1-3A will tease your eyes, or more precisely, your brain. Look at this cube for a while, and you see that its perspective changes suddenly. Sometimes you look at it from the top right angle (see figures 1-3B), but then you look at it from the bottom left corner (see figures 1-3C).

p44.original: 图1-3 内克尔立方体的不同视角
p44.en: Figure 1-3 Different perspectives of the Negar Cube

p45.original: 注：持续注视图1-3A。过了一会儿，它似乎改变了我们的视角？心理学如何帮助我们理解这一现象呢？
p45.en: Note: Keep looking at figures 1-3A. After a while, it seems to have changed our perspective? How can psychology help us understand this phenomenon?

p46.original: 第一次你可能需要一点时间才能看出立方体的变化。但是一旦你发现视角可以变化，你就会情不自禁地变换视角，变换成哪种视角似乎是随机的。试着把这个立方体给几个朋友看看，问问他们看到了什么。他们是否和你一样也看到了变换的视角？
p46.en: For the first time, you may need a little time to see the changes in the cube. But once you find out that you can change your perspective, you can't help but change it, which one seems random. Try showing this cube to a few friends and ask them what they saw. Did they see a change of perspective like you?

p47.original: 这一现象并不是由心理学家发现的。这是一位瑞士地理学家路易·内克尔（Louis Necker）在约200年前在显微镜下观察立方体水晶时首次发现的。尽管起源于此，神奇的内克尔立方体仍阐明了与心理学学习相关的两个重点。
p47.en: This phenomenon is not detected by psychologists. This was the first time that Louis Necker, a Swiss geographer, had observed a cube crystal under a microscope some 200 years ago. Despite its origins, the magic Necker Cube articulates two priorities related to psychological learning.

p48.original: 1. 内克尔立方体很好地阐释了冯特和他的学生最早创造的内省法。你会发现，我们唯一能够证明内克尔立方体在我们的大脑中改变了角度的方法就是：让人们看着立方体，报告他们看到了什么。那么为什么这对心理学很重要呢？只有最顽固的行为主义者才会否认看着立方体的人在精神层面发生了什么。事实上，内克尔立方体证明了我们会给感觉添加意义，这一过程被称为知觉。
p48.en: 1. The Nekel Cube gives a good illustration of the first internal law created by Fengt and his students. And you'll find that the only way we can prove that the Necker Cube has changed its angle in our brain is to show people what they see. So why is it important for psychology? Only the most stubborn activists can deny what happens at the mental level to those who look at the cube. In fact, the Necker Cube proves that we are going to add meaning to the feeling, a process known as consciousness.

p49.original: 2. 内克尔立方体可以用来隐喻心理学的多元视角。就像观察立方体的正确方法不止一个，心理学中也不存在能给我们关于行为和心理过程的全部“真相”的单一视角。换句话说，如果我们想充分理解心理学，我们必须在多个视角之间来回变换。
p49.en: 2. The Nekl Cube can be used as a metaphor for the pluralist perspective of psychology. Just as there is more than one way to observe the cube, there is no single perspective in psychology that gives us the full “truth” about behaviour and psychological processes. In other words, if we want to fully understand psychology, we have to change from perspective to perspective.

p50.original: 1.4.3 格式塔的反应：“整体，而非局部”
p50.en: 1.4.3 Reactions from the format towers: “integrity, not partial”

p51.original: 在20世纪早期，德国是孕育心理学兴趣和研究的温床。一个著名的理论家团体反对结构主义者强调意识元素的看法，这群人认为意识远远超出了简单的感官体验，并认为我们的体验不能被简化为一组离散的元素。这些后来以格式塔心理学家（gestalt psychologists）闻名的人，当时专注于意识经验的整体，而不是各部分的总和，并且试图理解我们是如何构造“知觉整体”的（见图1-4，顺便一提，格式塔在德语中是“整体”或“结构”的意思）。比如，我们如何从线条、形状、颜色和纹理中形成对一张脸的感知？
p51.en: In the early twentieth century, Germany was a hotbed for the development of psychological interest and research. A well-known ideologue group rejects the idea of structuralists emphasizing the element of consciousness, who believe that awareness goes far beyond simple sensory experiences and that our experiences cannot be reduced to a discrete set of elements. These were later known as gestalt psychologists, who were focused on the whole of consciousness experience rather than on the sum of the parts, and tried to understand how we constructed the “conscious whole” (see figure 1-4, by the way, the form tower in German means “the whole” or “structure”). How, for example, do we develop a sense of a face from lines, shapes, colours and textures?

p52.original: 图1-4 格式塔心理学：整体多于部分之和
p52.en: Figure 1-4 Formatary Tower Psychology: More than part of the total

p53.original: 注：你看到了什么？尽管这些线条没有完全相连，但我们的大脑在不知不觉间填补了空白，所以大多数人都能看到一只熊。这说明了格式塔封闭原则，以及格式塔理论家的信念，即意识经验的整体不仅仅是各部分的简单相加。
p53.en: Note: What do you see? Although these lines are not fully connected, our brain fills a gap without realizing it, so most people can see a bear. This illustrates the principle of the closure of the form towers and the belief of the form tower theorists that the whole of the conscious experience is more than a simple sum of parts.

p54.original: 1.4.4 詹姆斯与机能主义者的反抗
p54.en: 1.4.4 The resistance of James and the functionalists

p55.original: 冯特的另一个最激烈的批评者是美国心理学家威廉·詹姆斯（William James），他认为结构主义的方法过于狭隘（詹姆斯还说它很无聊——这让他和冯特之间原本就很紧张的关系雪上加霜）。詹姆斯认为，心理学应该包括意识的功能，而不仅仅是它的结构。詹姆斯的心理学派[2]因此被称为机能主义（functionalism）（Fancher，1979）。
p55.en: Another of Font's most violent critics was the American psychologist William James, who thought that the structuralist approach was too narrow (James also said it was boring — which made his relationship with Font so tense that he was already nervous). According to James, psychology should include the function of consciousness, not just its structure. James ' psychology [2] is thus known as functionalism (Fancher, 1979).

p56.original: 詹姆斯和他的追随者发现查尔斯·达尔文的想法远比冯特的思想有趣。和达尔文一样，詹姆斯也对情绪以及情绪与身体和行为的关系有很浓厚的兴趣（不像冯特的理论体系那样只把情绪视作意识的一个元素）。他也喜欢达尔文对于生物体适应环境的强调。詹姆斯因此提出，心理学应该解释人们如何适应或无法适应实验室之外的现实世界的情况。
p56.en: James and his followers found the idea of Charles Darwin far more interesting than that of Font. Like Darwin, James has a strong interest in emotions and their relationship to body and behavior (as opposed to the vonter system of theory, which sees emotions only as an element of consciousness). He also likes Darwin's emphasis on living organisms adapting to the environment. As a result, James argued that psychology should explain how people are or cannot adapt to the reality of the world outside the laboratory.

p57.original: 后来，机能主义者成为第一批应用心理学家（applied psychologists）——研究如何运用心理学来改善人类生活。詹姆斯本人在学习“习惯”的养成、宗教心理学和教学方面著有大量作品。他也是第一位要求学生评价自己的美国教授（Fancher，1979）。他的追随者约翰·杜威（John Dewey）发起了“进步主义教育”运动，强调从做中学，而不是仅仅听课和死记硬背。
p57.en: Later on, the functionalists became the first applied psychologists - to study how psychology can be used to improve human life. James himself has a great deal of work in the field of “customary” development, religious psychology and teaching. He was also the first American professor to ask students to evaluate himself (Fancher 1979). His followers, John Dewey, launched the “Education for Progress” campaign, emphasizing secondary school, not just listening to lessons and dying.

p58.original: 内省法是结构主义与机能主义的共识。但讽刺的是，它们的一致观点也是它们最大的弱点：内省法是主观的，导致他们的心理学派很容易被批评为不是真正的科学。解决这个问题花了半个多世纪的时间，通过不同学科的专家合作，最终形成了现代认知视角。
p58.en: Internal law is the consensus between structuralism and functionalism. But ironically, their unanimous view is also their greatest weakness: internal law is subjective, and their psychology can easily be criticized as not true science. It took more than half a century to resolve the problem, and through the collaboration of experts from different disciplines, it eventually developed a modern cognitive perspective.

p60.original: 计算机成了心智的新隐喻，其发展势不可当地将心理学推向了新的综合：现代认知视角（cognitive perspective）。基于结构主义、机能主义和格式塔心理学的传统，这一视角也强调认知和心理活动，如知觉、理解、预期、信念和记忆。从这个角度来看，一个人的思想和行为都是对个人经历的知觉和理解的独特的认知模式的结果。
p60.en: Computers have become new metaphors of mind, and their development has led to an inappropriate shift in psychology to a new synthesis: a modern cognitive perspective. This perspective also emphasizes cognitive and psychological activities, such as consciousness, understanding, anticipation, conviction and memory, based on a tradition of structuralism, functionalism and formal psychology. From this perspective, one's thoughts and behaviour are the result of unique patterns of perception and understanding of one's experience.

p61.original: 与前人相比，今日的认知视角拥有更客观的观察方法。这要感谢脑成像技术的惊人进步，使科学家能够观测各种心理过程中的大脑活动。例如，对记忆的运作方式感兴趣的认知心理学家已经确定了某些与常见记忆障碍相关的大脑模式——并且发现了增强记忆力的方法。认知心理学这个领域也能帮助我们理解很多经常干扰理性思维的思维偏差。
p61.en: Today's cognitive perspective has a more objective approach to observation than that of previous generations. This is thanks to the remarkable advances in brain imaging technology, which enables scientists to observe brain activity in all psychological processes. For example, cognitive psychologists interested in how memory works have identified certain brain models associated with common memory disorders - and found ways to enhance memory. The area of cognitive psychology can also help us understand many of the mental biases that often interfere with rational thinking.

p62.original: 认知心理学家会如何解释拖延？你是怎么想的？
p62.en: How would cognitive psychologists explain delays? What do you think?

p63.original: 首先，他们认为，拖延者通常会低估项目完成所需的时间——这说明了预期在我们行为模式中的作用。此外，如果拖延者只记得他们曾经拖延过却依然按时完成了项目的经历，却忘记了错过截止期限的经历，他们可能是证实性偏差的受害者。最后，把事情拖延到最后一分钟的人可能不会把自己的行为解读为问题——也许他们相信在压力下才能把工作做得最好。通过这些途径，认知心理学解释了影响拖延和其他人类行为的内在思维过程。
p63.en: First, they believe that procrastination usually underestimates the time required to complete the project — an indication of the expected role in our mode of behaviour. Moreover, if those who delay remember only their experience of delaying but still completing the project on time, and forget their missed deadlines, they may be victims of corroborating bias. Finally, those who delay things to the last minute may not interpret their behaviour as a problem — perhaps they believe that under pressure they can do the best they can. In these ways, cognitive psychology explains the internal thinking processes that influence delays and other human behaviour.

p66.original: 总结在20世纪出现的心理学视角。
p66.en: Summarizing the psychological perspective that emerged in the twentieth century.

p67.original: 到了20世纪，心理学领域才开始真正成长。早期的认知理论家，如冯特和詹姆斯，为新的观点铺平了道路，如行为视角，新的观点旨在利用科学原理研究心理学。不要忘记，格式塔学派同样打开了从更整体的视角（如发展视角、全人视角）进一步研究人类行为的大门。20世纪中叶，心理学家开始认识到文化和我们的情境环境在影响我们行为方面的重要性。下面让我们更详细地考察这4个视角。
p67.en: It was only in the twentieth century that the area of psychology began to grow. Early cognitive theorists, such as Font and James, have paved the way for new perspectives, such as behavioural perspectives, aimed at using scientific principles to study psychology. It is important to remember that the form towers also open the door to further study of human behaviour from a more holistic perspective (e.g. development perspective, human perspective). In the middle of the twentieth century, psychologists began to recognize the importance of culture and our context in influencing our behaviour. Let us look at these four perspectives in more detail.

p68.original: 1.5.1 行为视角关注可观察的和可测量的行为
p68.en: 1.5.1 Behavioural perspectives focus on observable and measurable behaviour

p69.original: 20世纪初，一个特别激进和活跃的群体出现了，他们被称为行为主义者，这些人因几乎与所有人的意见相左而声名鹊起。他们最著名的观点是，心智根本不应该是心理学的一部分！行为主义运动的早期领导人约翰·华生（John Watson）认为，真正的客观的心理学只应该研究可观察到的事件：来自环境的物理刺激和生物体的外显反应。华生说，行为主义（behaviorism）是研究行为和影响行为的可测量的环境条件的科学。
p69.en: At the beginning of the twentieth century, a particularly radical and active group emerged, known as activists, known for being in opposition to almost everyone's views. Their most famous point is that mind is not even a part of psychology! The early leader of the behaviorist movement, John Watson, argued that true objective psychology should only look at observable events: physical irritation from the environment and the appearance of organisms. According to Watson, behavioralism is the science of measurable environmental conditions that study behaviour and influence behaviour.

p70.original: 行为主义者为什么反对将心理过程——比如内省——作为科学研究的一个可行领域？另一位有影响力的行为主义心理学家B. F.斯金纳（B.F. Skinner）提出，具有诱惑性的概念“心智”把心理学引入了死循环，这可能是对行为主义观点的最好说明了。他认为，心智是一个非常主观，甚至无法被证明存在的东西（Skinner，1990）（想一想，你能证明自己有心智吗）。斯金纳还揶揄道：“一个由来已久的关键错误是相信我们做出行为时的感受是我们行为的原因。”（Skinner，1989）因此，对于行为主义者来说，一个人的思想或情绪是无关紧要的——只有行为才能被可靠地观察和测量。因此，行为学家们会将无害的白色老鼠和突然发出的巨大声响匹配在一起，观察小孩是否会开始躲避白鼠，而不是研究“恐惧”这一情绪。重要的是，行为主义者反对对外在行为（如躲避）的内在表征（如恐惧）做出任何主观推测。
p70.en: Why do behaviouralists oppose psychological processes — such as the interior — as a viable area for scientific research? Another influential behavioural psychologist, B. F. Skinner, suggested that the seductive concept of “spiritual mind” introduced psychology into the circle of death, perhaps the best illustration of a behavioral view. He believes that mind is a very subjective, even unproven, thing (Skinner, 1990) (Think, can you prove that you have a mind). Skinner also said: “A long-standing key mistake is to believe that what we feel when we do it is the reason for our actions. Thus, for behaviorists, one's mind or emotion is irrelevant — only behaviour can be reliably observed and measured. Therefore, behaviouralists match harmless white rats with sudden, huge noises to see whether children will start avoiding rats rather than studying the feeling of “fear”. Importantly, behaviouralists oppose any subjective speculation by external actors about the intrinsic signs of behaviour (e.g. e. e. e. e. e. e. e. e. e. e. e., fear).

p71.original: 我们可以这样总结行为主义激进派的新观点：
p71.en: This is how we can sum up the new ideas of the activist radicals:

p72.original: 心理学的研究对象应该仅限于可观察的行为和影响行为的环境刺激。
p72.en: Psychological research should be limited to detectable behaviour and environmental incentives that influence behaviour.

p73.original: 行为视角（behavioral perspective）关注我们的行为是如何被其结果所改变的，比如，当一个孩子因为说“谢谢”而受到表扬，或者一个成年人因良好的工作表现而获得加薪。行为主义者为我们深入理解影响人类学习的各种环境力量做出了巨大贡献，他们还为我们提供了通过改变环境来改变行为的有效策略（Alferink，2005；Roediger，2004）。
p73.en: Behavioral perspective focuses on how our behaviour is changed by the results, for example, when a child is praised for saying “thank you”, or when an adult is paid a salary for good performance. Activists have contributed significantly to our understanding of the environmental forces that influence human learning, and they have also provided us with effective strategies to change behaviour by changing the environment (Alferink, 2005); Roediger, 2004.

p74.original: 你认为关注奖励与惩罚的行为主义者会怎样解释拖延？
p74.en: How do you think the activists who care about rewards and punishments explain the delay?

p75.original: 思考一下，推迟一些你不想做的事情能带来什么好处：你可以花时间做一些你喜欢的事情，而不是做那些可怕的工作，你可以立即得到满足。然后，当你在最后一刻解决问题时，若你在这种紧要关头成功搞定了它，胜利的喜悦会是你的奖励！拖延这种行为很难改变也就不足为奇了。幸运的是，行为主义者也提供了一些克服这种令人烦恼的行为模式的有效策略。
p75.en: Think about the benefits of postponing something you don't want to do: you can spend time doing something you like, not doing something terrible, and you can get it right away. And then, when you solve the problem at the last minute, if you succeed at this critical juncture, the joy of victory will be your reward! It is not surprising that such acts are difficult to change. Fortunately, behaviouralists have also provided effective strategies to overcome this troubling pattern of behaviour.

p77.original: 运用奖励来做出一些积极的改变
p77.en: Using incentives to make some positive changes.

p78.original: 描述一个令你烦恼的行为得到奖励的场景。列出一个可作为替代的、更理想的行为，以及一个你为了改善行为而给自己的奖励。
p78.en: Describes a scene where you're rewarded for your troubled behavior. Lists an alternative, more desirable behaviour, and a reward you give yourself to improve your behavior.

p79.original: 1.5.2 发展视角强调我们如何改变
p79.en: 1.5.2 Development perspective emphasizes how we change

p80.original: 在我们的人生经历中，唯一不变的就是改变。从发展视角（developmental perspective）来看，心理变化是遗传基因与环境影响相互作用的结果。但先天（遗传）和后天（环境）哪个更重要呢？正如我们所看到的，生物心理学家强调先天遗传，而行为主义者则强调后天教养。发展心理学是两股力量交互的地方。
p80.en: The only thing that's ever changed in our life experience is change. From a development perspective, mental change is the result of interactions between genetic and environmental impacts. But what is more important about congenital (genetic) and acquired (environmental) conditions? As we have seen, biopsychologists emphasize congenital genes, while behaviouralists emphasize acquired culture. Development psychology is where two forces interact.

p81.original: 定义发展视角的重要思想如下：
p81.en: The following are important ideas for defining a development perspective:

p82.original: 随着时间的推移，在遗传和环境的共同影响下，人会以可预测的方式变化。
p82.en: Over time, people change in a predictable manner under the combined effects of genetic and environmental influences.

p83.original: 换句话说，人在一生中的不同时期，思想和行为会有所不同。生理层面，我们可以直观地看到人的发展，比如，成长期、青春期以及更年期。心理层面，发展包括语言的习得、逻辑思维以及在人生的不同时期承担不同的角色。发展心理学家可能不会为一个拖延的青少年感到惊讶。相反，他们可能会把拖延看作那个年龄的正常行为，因为青少年还在学习如何兼顾多种责任，如何准确估计完成这些事情需要多长时间，同时还要应对自己身体和社交世界的变化。
p83.en: In other words, at different times in a person's life, ideas and behaviour will be different. At the biological level, we can visualize human development, such as long-term, adolescence and menopause. At the psychological level, development includes language learning, logical thinking and different roles in different times of life. The development of psychologists may not surprise a delayed adolescent. Rather, they may regard delays as normal behaviour at that age, as adolescents are also learning how to balance multiple responsibilities and how to accurately estimate how long it takes to do these things, while also coping with changes in their bodies and in the social world.

p84.original: 过去，发展心理学的大部分研究都聚焦于儿童——一部分原因是他们变化得很快且可以预测。然而，当我们发现发展过程贯穿我们人生始终时，发展心理学家就开始增加了对青少年和成年人的研究。
p84.en: In the past, much of the research on development psychology focused on children — partly because they were fast-changing and predictable. However, when we find that the process of development runs through our lives, the development of psychologists begins to increase research into adolescents and adults.

p85.original: 为人父母者都知道“可怕的两岁”，这是一个情绪爆发更频繁的年龄。发展心理学家解释说，孩子在这个年龄时，其独立的意愿增强，但其大脑有效处理挫折的能力却有限，二者叠加就自然形成了这样的结果。
p85.en: Parents are aware of the “gruesome two-year-old” age, which is the age of more frequent emotional eruptions. The development psychologist explained that children at that age had increased their independence, but their brain had limited capacity to deal effectively with setbacks, and that the combination of the two had naturally resulted in such an outcome.

p86.original: 这个少年正在做对他的年龄而言正常的冒险行为。发展心理学家指出，在我们的青少年时期，我们大脑的理性部分还没发展出控制冲动的能力，这解释了为什么青少年经常冒险。
p86.en: The young man was engaged in a normal risk-taking behaviour for his age. Development psychologists have pointed out that, during our adolescence, the rational part of our brain has not developed the capacity to control impulses, which explains why adolescents often take risks.

p87.original: 1.5.3 社会文化视角将我们和他人联结起来
p87.en: 1.5.3 Sociocultural perspectives connect us to others

p88.original: 谁能否认人们彼此间有着巨大的影响呢？社会文化视角（sociocultural perspective）将社会影响的观点安置在了舞台中央。从这个角度来看，社会心理学家探索了喜欢、爱、偏见、攻击、服从和从众的心理之谜。此外，许多人对这些社会过程在不同文化中的差异感兴趣。
p88.en: Who can deny that people have a huge influence on each other? The socio-cultural perspective (social perspective) places the social impact perspective at the centre of the stage. From this perspective, social psychologists explore the puzzles of love, love, prejudice, assault, obedience and public opinion. In addition, many people are interested in the differences in these social processes across cultures.

p89.original: 本书作者之一，菲利普·津巴多博士是一位研究“情境的力量”在控制人类行为中的作用的社会心理学家。
p89.en: One of the authors of this book, Dr. Philip Zimbado, is a social psychologist studying the role of “the power of the situation” in controlling human behaviour.

p90.original: 文化（culture）是人类语言、信仰、习俗、价值观和传统的复杂融合体，对我们每个人都有着深远的影响。我们不仅可以在比较不同大洲的人时看到文化的作用，也可以在比较诸如美国圣地亚哥的加利福尼亚-墨西哥文化和明尼苏达州的斯堪的纳维亚文化中的人时看到文化的作用。早期心理学对文化的忽视，部分是由于科学心理学源自欧洲和北美洲，那里的大多数心理学家都生活和工作在相似的文化条件下（Lonner & Malpass，1994；Segall et al.，1998）。今天，这一视角已被拓宽：在全世界50万名心理学家中，只有不到一半的人在美国生活和工作，而在非欧洲和北美洲的国家中，人们对心理学的兴趣与日俱增（Pawlik & d’Ydewalle，1996；Rosenzweig，1992，1999）。尽管如此，我们的许多心理学知识依然带有欧美特色。跨文化心理学家（cross-cultural psychologists）承认存在这一偏差，开始执行一项艰巨的任务，即重新审视跨越文化和种族界线的心理学“定理”（Cole，2006）。
p90.en: Culture is a complex combination of human languages, beliefs, customs, values and traditions that has far-reaching implications for us all. We can see the role of culture not only in comparing people on different continents, but also in comparing people in California-Mexico and Scandinavian cultures such as Santiago de America and Minnesota. Early psychological neglect of culture is partly due to the fact that scientific psychology originates in Europe and North America, where most psychologists live and work under similar cultural conditions (Lonner & Malpass, 1994); Segal et al., 1998. Today, this perspective has been broadened: fewer than half of the world's 500,000 psychologists live and work in the United States, while in countries other than Europe and North America there is growing interest in psychology (Pawlik & d ' Ydewalle, 1996); Rosenzweig, 1992, 1999. Nevertheless, much of our psychological knowledge still has a European-American character. Cross-cultural psychologists acknowledge this bias and begin the difficult task of re-examining the psychological “theorem” across cultural and ethnic lines (Coles, 2006).

p91.original: 当然，社会文化观点的支持者并不否认遗传、学习甚至无意识过程的作用。反倒是他们给心理学带来了一个强大的附加概念：情境的力量。从这个角度看，人所处的社会和文化环境有时会胜过所有其他影响行为的因素。比如，某些文化非常强调按时完成任务，这反过来会影响该文化中个体的行为（如拖延）。
p91.en: Of course, supporters of sociocultural views do not deny the role of genetic, learning and even unconscious processes. Instead, they bring a powerful additional concept to psychology: the power of the situation. From this perspective, the social and cultural environment in which a person lives sometimes outweighs all other factors influencing behaviour. For example, certain cultures place great emphasis on the timely fulfilment of mandates, which in turn affects the behaviour of individuals in that culture, such as delays.

p94.original: 写出一个最近发生的、情境或文化因素干扰你及时关注项目的例子。
p94.en: Writes an example of a recent situation or cultural factor that interferes with your timely attention to the project.

p95.original: 1.5.4 全人视角重新强调整体

p96.original: 20世纪初，维也纳的医生西格蒙德·弗洛伊德（Sigmund Freud）和他的追随者对冯特和结构主义提出了新的挑战，他们发展出一种治疗精神障碍的方法，这种方法基于另一个激进的观点：
p96.en: At the beginning of the twentieth century, doctors in Vienna, Sigmund Freud, and his followers, presented new challenges to vonter and structuralism by developing a cure for mental disorders based on another radical view:

p97.original: 人格和精神障碍主要源于意识之外的无意识的心理过程。
p97.en: Personal and mental disorders arise mainly from unconscious psychological processes outside of consciousness.

p98.original: 虽然弗洛伊德并不是第一个提出我们无法察觉到某些心理过程的人，但结构主义和机能主义都没有考虑过无意识过程支配人格且导致精神障碍的可能。此外，弗洛伊德的精神分析理论旨在解释完整的人，而不像其他心理学流派那样，仅解释某些组成部分（如注意、知觉、记忆、行为或情绪）。他的目标是用一个宏大的理论来解释思想和行为的各个方面。
p98.en: Although Freud was not the first to suggest that we could not detect certain psychological processes, neither structuralism nor functionalism considered the possibility of unconscious processes taking over personality and leading to mental disorders. In addition, Freud's psychoanalytical theory is designed to explain the whole human being, not just certain components (e.g. attention, perception, memory, behaviour or emotions) as other psychological schools do. His goal was to interpret all aspects of thought and behaviour with an ambitious theory.

p99.original: 心理动力学（psychodynamic psychology） 弗洛伊德可能是一位难以相处的导师，这使他的许多追随者与他分道扬镳，去发展他们各自的理论。我们使用的精神动力这个术语既包括弗洛伊德的观点，也包括基于他的观点诞生的其他新弗洛伊德学派的观点。弗洛伊德的观点是，心理（psyche），尤其是无意识心理，是人格能量（dynamics）的蓄水池。根据心理动力学的观点，这种能量是我们的动力。
p99.en: Psychodynamic psychology Freud may be a hard-to-reach mentor, leading many of his followers to separate from him and to develop their respective theories. We use the term "spiritual drive " to include both the Freudian perspective and that of other new Freudian schools born on the basis of his viewpoint. Freud's view is that the psychosis (psyche), especially unconscious psychology, is the reservoir of dynamics. From the point of view of psychodynamics, this energy is our power.

p100.original: 心理动力学方法的首个也是最著名的代表人物当然是西格蒙德·弗洛伊德，他的体系被称为精神分析（psychoanalysis）。这一体系最初被设想为治疗精神障碍的医疗技术，它强调对梦境、口误（也就是所谓的“弗洛伊德口误”）的分析，强调一种被称为自由联想的技术，以收集被意识压抑的无意识冲突和“不被认可的”欲望的线索。比如，精神分析师可能会把一个人自暴自弃的行为——比如拖延——解释为对失败的无意识恐惧。
p100.en: The first and most prominent representative of psychodynamics is, of course, Sigmund Freud, whose system is known as psychoanalysis (psychoanalysis). This system, originally conceived as a medical technique for the treatment of mental disorders, emphasizes the analysis of dreams, verbal errors (so-called “Freud verbal errors”) and a technique known as free association to gather clues about unconscious conflicts and “unrecognized” desires that are suppressed by consciousness. For example, psychoanalysts may interpret a person's self-absorption — for example, delay — as an unconscious fear of failure.

p101.original: 和弗洛伊德一样，大多数精神分析师都是精神病学专业的，并且是接受过弗洛伊德方法高级培训的医生。但是，有志于对完整的人进行解释的不止精神分析从业者，还有两个学派也对全面了解人格感兴趣，它们是人本主义心理学和特质与气质心理学。这里，我们把这三个心理学派均归类于全人视角（whole-person perspectives）
p101.en: Like Freud, most psychoanalysts are specializing in psychiatry and are doctors with advanced training in Freud methodology. However, there are not only psychoanalysts who are interested in interpreting the whole person, but also two schools that are interested in a comprehensive understanding of the person, namely, the humanist psychology and the ethos and aerobic psychology. Here, we've classified all three psychology factions into a whole-person perspective.

p102.original: 人本主义心理学（humanistic psychology）精神分析强调无意识中“恶”的力量，而人本主义心理学却选了一条不同的道路。
p102.en: The psychoanalysis of humanism emphasizes the power of “evil” unconsciously, while the humanistic psychology chooses a different path.

p103.original: 他们的全新观点强调人类天性中积极的一面，包括人类能力、成长和潜能。
p103.en: Their new perspective emphasizes the positive side of human nature, including human capabilities, growth and potential.

p104.original: 这幅漫画展示了弗洛伊德口误，说明我们试图隐藏的想法或感受有时会不小心脱口而出。这样，我们的潜意识就暴露了。
p104.en: This cartoon shows Freud's mistakes, suggesting that we try to hide our thoughts or feelings sometimes unwittingly. So our subconscious is exposed.

p105.original: 在亚伯拉罕·马斯洛（Abraham Maslow）和卡尔·罗杰斯（Carl Rogers）等人本主义者的领导下，他们提出了一个人性模型，认为人类具有成长和向善的先天需求，并强调人们可以自由行使意志，做出影响他们生活和成长的选择（Kendler，2005）。
p105.en: Under the leadership of its ownists, such as Abraham Maslow and Carl Rogers, they have proposed a model of humanity that recognizes the birthright of human beings to grow and to be good and emphasizes that people can freely exercise their will to make choices that affect their lives and growth (Kendler, 2005).

p106.original: 人本主义者认为，自我概念和自尊对人的思想、情绪和行为有非常大的影响，而思想、情绪和行为最终会影响你的潜能的发展。因此，从这个角度来看，拖延可能是由低自尊驱动的——或者相反，如果拖延者相信他可以比实际完成工作的速度更快，那就是由过高的自尊驱动的。无论是哪种驱动方式，行为都可以追溯到人对自己的信念。与心理动力学一样，人本主义心理学也对咨询和心理治疗实践产生了重大影响。
p106.en: The humanists believe that self-image and self-esteem have a very strong influence on people's thoughts, emotions and behaviours, which ultimately affect the development of your potential. From this point of view, therefore, delays may be driven by low self-esteem — or, conversely, by excessive self-esteem if the delayr believes that he can do his job faster than he actually does. In any way, behaviour can be traced back to a person's belief in himself. Like psychokinetics, humanistic psychology has had a significant impact on the practice of counselling and psychotherapy.

p107.original: 特质与气质心理学（trait andtemperamentpsychology） 古希腊人预言了许多现代思想，他们提出人格由4种体液支配：多血质、黏液质、抑郁质和胆汁质。根据占主导地位的体液的不同，人的性格可能是乐观的（多血质主导），迟缓谨慎的（黏液质主导），忧郁的（抑郁质主导），或易怒且有攻击性的（胆汁质主导）。
p107.en: Trait and temperamentpsychology, the ancient Greeks predicted many modern ideas, suggesting that the personality was dominated by four types of body fluid: polyblood, mucous, depressed, and cholesterol. Depending on the dominant body fluid, the human personality may be optimistic (multi-blood dominated), slow and cautious (mixed dominated), depressed (depressive dominated), or angry and aggressive (coloured dominated).

p108.original: 当然，我们现在不再买古希腊人的类型学的账。但他们的人格特质理念在今天的特质与气质心理学中仍然具有活力。这个学派的基本观点是：
p108.en: Of course, we're not buying old Greek type books now. But their idea of personality is still alive in today's quality and aerobic psychology. The basic point of this school is:

p109.original: 人与人之间的差异源自个人持久的特征和内在的倾向性，也就是特质和气质。
p109.en: Differences between human beings stem from the enduring characteristics and intrinsic preferences of individuals, i.e. the characteristics and the quality of individuals.

p110.original: 你可能听说过内向和外向这样的特质，它们似乎成了人性的基本特征。其他特质心理学家在世界各地的人们身上发现的其他特征，包括焦虑感或幸福感、对新体验的开放性、宜人性和尽责性。一些心理学家还提出，我们在一个更基础的层面上存在差异，这个层面叫作气质，它被认为可以用来解释新生儿（包括成年人）的不同性情。
p110.en: You may have heard of the traits of inward and outward orientation, which seem to be the basic features of humanity. Other features found by other quality psychologists in people around the world include anxiety or happiness, openness to new experiences, humanity and due diligence. Some psychologists have also suggested that there are differences at a more basic level, called the ethos, which is considered to be used to explain the different sexual characteristics of newborns, including adults.

p111.original: 特质与气质心理学家可能会从一个人尽责性的程度来解释拖延症。举例来说，一个尽责性高的人——换句话说，对待承诺非常认真的人——就不太可能拖延。而习惯拖延的人，即使没有按时完成任务，他们也不会有特别大的压力，也不会担心被贴上尽责性低、性格懒散的标签（这也就解释了为什么他们不会有特别大的压力）。应当说，这些性格特点至少有一部分是天生的，它们在不同时间、情境下具有相对稳定性。
p111.en: Characteristic and gaseous psychologists may explain the delay in terms of a person's due diligence. For example, it is unlikely that a person with a high level of due diligence — in other words, a person who is very serious about his commitment — will be able to delay. Those who are habitually delayed, even if they do not complete their tasks on time, will not be under particular pressure and will not fear being labeled as being insensitive and lazy (which explains why they will not be under particular pressure). It should be said that at least some of these character characteristics are natural, and that they are relatively stable at different times and in different circumstances.

p112.original: 1.6 心理学视角：你工具箱中的6种工具
p112.en: 1.6 Psychological perspective: six tools in your toolbox

p114.original: 将心理学视角应用于自己的行为。
p114.en: Applying a psychological perspective to one's own behaviour.

p115.original: 综合起来，这6个视角对于我们全面理解人类行为都起着重要作用。正如我们在拖延的例子中看到的，多个视角都可以被合理地应用于任一行为——很少出现单一视角就能充分解释行为的情况。（然而，我们必须补充一点，解释某种行为不代表为它的正当性辩护。反之，这可以为克服有问题的行为提供线索，或者有助于我们理解他人的行为。）在几乎所有情况下，我们都需要运用多个视角来全面理解人类行为的原因。综合起来，它们构成了心理学的多元视角，每一个视角都将成为你理解人类行为的“心理学工具箱”中的重要工具。就像木匠工具箱中的各种工具是建造房屋所必需的一样，当你解读人类行为时，这里的每一个视角都是一种独特且不可或缺的工具。
p115.en: Taken together, these six perspectives play an important role in our overall understanding of human behaviour. As we have seen in the case of delays, multiple perspectives can be reasonably applied to any act — rarely a single perspective adequately explains the act. (However, we must add that an explanation of an act does not represent a defence to its legitimacy. On the contrary, it can provide clues to overcome problematic behaviour or help us understand the behaviour of others. In almost all cases, we need to apply multiple perspectives to a comprehensive understanding of the causes of human behaviour. Taken together, they constitute a multifaceted psychological perspective, each of which will be an important tool in your “psychological toolbox” of understanding human behaviour. Just as the tools in the carpenter's toolbox are necessary to build a house, every perspective here is a unique and indispensable tool when you interpret human behaviour.

p116.original: 试一试 心理学视角的应用
p116.en: Try it. The application of a psychological perspective.

p117.original: 通过将6个心理学视角应用于生活中令你感兴趣的行为，你会在解读人的行为起因方面变得更有经验、更准确。
p117.en: By applying six psychological perspectives to behaviours that are of interest to you in life, you will become more experienced and accurate in interpreting the causes of human behaviour.

p118.original: 为什么有些人会有恐怖或暴力行为？
p118.en: Why would some people be afraid or violent?

p119.original: 是什么导致了恋情中的不忠？
p119.en: What led to infidelity in relationships?

p120.original: 当众发言时，是什么原因让人感到紧张？
p120.en: What makes people nervous when speaking in public?

p122.original: 请思考其中的某个问题，或者你自己提出新的问题。你能用4个以上的心理学视角来解释这种行为吗？如果可以，说明你已经开始理解心理学多元视角的重要性了。
p122.en: Please think about one of those issues or ask yourself new ones. Can you explain this behavior with more than four psychological perspectives? If you can, it means you've begun to understand the importance of a pluralist perspective of psychology.

p125.original: 指出一个令你困惑的行为，可以是你自己的，也可以是别人的。请用两个以上的心理学视角来解释这一行为。
p125.en: Point out a behavior that confuses you, which can be yours or someone else. Please explain this behaviour with more than two psychological perspectives.

p126.original: 心理学很有用 心理学的变迁

p127.original: 现代心理学是一个不断变化的领域。近几十年来，生物、认知和发展视角在心理学中占据了主导地位。曾经彼此冲突的视角越来越多地开始建立联系且形成合力：我们现在可以看到“认知行为主义者”或“进化发展心理学家”等新的、奇怪的混合心理学家。与此同时，几乎所有心理学流派都渴望与神经科学建立联系，神经科学正快速成为心理学领域的支柱之一。
p127.en: Modern psychology is an evolving field. In recent decades, biological, cognitive and developmental perspectives have dominated psychology. Increasingly, conflicting perspectives are beginning to connect and forge synergies: we can now see new, strange combinations of psychologists, such as “cognitive behaviorists” or “psychologists for evolutionary development”. At the same time, almost all psychological genres are eager to establish links with the neuroscience, which is fast becoming one of the pillars of psychology.

p128.original: 我们还希望你能注意到女性心理学家和少数族裔心理学家占比的明显变化。少数族裔——尤其是亚裔、非裔和拉丁裔——心理学家的人数正在增加，在新增的心理学博士中，他们的占比为25%左右（APA Center for Workforce Studies，2010）。更为惊人的事实是女性成了心理学界的多数群体。《美国科学家名人录》（American Men of Science）（这个名字没有讽刺的意思）上的数据显示，1906年，美国心理学家中的女性占比只有12%。1921年，这一比例上升到20%。今天，在每年新增的心理学博士中，女性的比例超过2/3（Cynkar，2007b；Kohout，2001）。尽管心理学领域的女性比例一直比其他科学领域中高，但性别偏见还是会阻碍其职业发展（Furumoto & Scarborough，1986）。例如，美国心理学的先驱之一G.斯坦利·霍尔（G. Stanley Hall）就曾断言，学术工作会损害女性的健康，甚至会使她们的生殖器官衰退。事实上，早在1905年，美国心理学会就选出了其史上第一位女性主席玛丽·惠顿·卡尔金斯（Mary Whiton Calkins）。表1-1列出了在心理学领域做出了重要贡献的女性。
p128.en: We would also like to draw your attention to the marked change in the proportion of female psychologists and those from ethnic minorities. The number of psychologists from ethnic minorities, especially Asians, Afro-Latins and Latinos, is increasing, and their share among the new PhDs is around 25 per cent (APA Center for Workforce Studies, 2010). It is even more striking that women are the majority of the psychological community. According to data from American Men of Science, a name no irony, the proportion of women among American psychologists was only 12 per cent in 1906. In 1921, this proportion rose to 20 per cent. Today, women account for more than 2/3 of the new PhDs each year (Cynkar, 2007b); Kohout, 2001. Although the percentage of women in psychology has been higher than in other scientific fields, gender bias still hinders their career development (Furumoto & Scarborough, 1986). For example, G. Stanley Hall, one of the pioneers of American psychology, had asserted that academic work could harm women's health and even degenerate their reproductive organs. Indeed, as early as 1905, the American Psychological Association elected Mary Wheton Calkins, its first female president in history. Table 1-1 lists women who have made important contributions in the field of psychology.

p129.original: 跨文化心理学家，如在肯尼亚的这位研究人员，为检验心理学知识的效度提供了重要数据。
p129.en: Cross-cultural psychologists, such as the researcher in Kenya, provide important data to test the effectiveness of psychological knowledge.

p130.original: 表1-1 女性对心理学的贡献举例
p130.en: Table 1-1 Examples of Women's Contribution to Psychology
